paths.description: Homepage/live-score listing and consent entry state; represents the primary results task.
Alternate sport listing template; represents sport/category listings.
World Cup competition template; represents league/tournament navigation.
Match detail template; represents the primary detail journey and mobile advertising state.
News article template; represents editorial content and share/discovery metadata.
Unknown route; represents HTTP/runtime failure recovery.

findings.summary: Reduced-motion preference does not stop persistent shimmer and pulse animations
findings.evidence: The prefers-reduced-motion evaluate probe found dozens of running 1.5 s placeholderShimmer animations and a running 1.2 s menuLiveIndicatorPulse while reduce was active.
findings.suggestedFix: Under @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce), remove non-essential shimmer/pulse animation or replace it with a static state.

findings.summary: Consent interstitial dominates the first view on result and match pages
findings.evidence: Desktop and mobile load screenshots show the OneTrust consent interface covering the primary results area; at 360x800 it consumes most of the viewport before scores can be read.
findings.suggestedFix: Use a compact, non-obscuring consent surface with equally clear accept/reject actions; defer detailed vendor disclosure to the preferences dialog.

findings.summary: Consent overlays use custom role=dialog containers rather than native dialog
findings.evidence: The platform probe counted 0 dialog elements, 0 popovers, and 2 role=dialog containers for consent UI.
findings.suggestedFix: Use native <dialog> for modal consent preferences, with native focus management and close behavior.

findings.summary: Advertising and chrome crowd the core match task on mobile
findings.evidence: The match mobile screenshot gives the top 227 px to three gambling advertisements and site chrome before match context, followed immediately by the consent wall.
findings.suggestedFix: Reserve the first mobile viewport for match identity/status and defer or collapse advertising below the primary task.

findings.summary: Mobile load performance is far outside good Core Web Vitals
findings.evidence: Lighthouse measured LCP 14.5 s, CLS 0.32, TBT 900 ms, and a performance score of 0.20.
findings.suggestedFix: Profile the LCP dependency chain, prioritise the LCP resource, reduce startup JavaScript, and reserve late content space; re-test on mobile.

findings.summary: Late content and unsized images create layout-instability risk
findings.evidence: Lighthouse measured CLS 0.32; the images probe found all 100 img elements lacked width and height attributes.
findings.suggestedFix: Set intrinsic width/height or aspect-ratio for every image and reserve stable slots for consent, ads, score rows, and fonts.

findings.summary: Startup JavaScript blocks the main thread
findings.evidence: Lighthouse measured 900 ms TBT; the mobile layout observers also captured 73-91 ms long tasks across home, match, and article templates.
findings.suggestedFix: Break long tasks, defer non-critical modules, and schedule score/analytics work by priority after the primary content is interactive.

findings.summary: The critical delivery path is fragmented across many assets
findings.evidence: HAR recorded 109 requests, 42 scripts, 37 stylesheets, 2.13 MB transferred, and many parser-inserted VeryHigh-priority stylesheets.
findings.suggestedFix: Consolidate critical CSS, defer template-specific styles/scripts, and shorten the LCP dependency chain while preserving cacheability.

findings.summary: Third-party and legacy script weight dominates the load
findings.evidence: HAR recorded 1.29 MB third-party transfer (67 requests), including 533 KB from Google Tag Manager and 174 KB from Facebook; first-party also ships both core and core_legacy bundles.
findings.suggestedFix: Gate analytics behind consent, remove redundant destinations and legacy bundles for capable browsers, and load optional integrations on demand.

findings.summary: The accessibility tree has semantic defects
findings.evidence: Lighthouse found prohibited ARIA attributes (3), untitled frames (3), one heading-order failure, and one visible-label/accessibility-name mismatch.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove prohibited ARIA, title every iframe, restore sequential headings, and ensure accessible names include visible labels.

findings.summary: Document assets include unsized and incorrectly proportioned images
findings.evidence: Lighthouse reported one incorrect image aspect ratio; the image probe found 100/100 images without intrinsic dimensions and one missing alt.
findings.suggestedFix: Correct aspect ratios, provide intrinsic dimensions, and add an appropriate alt (or empty alt for decorative imagery).

findings.summary: A JavaScript exception is logged during page load
findings.evidence: Lighthouse captured TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading getIdent) at the main document.
findings.suggestedFix: Guard the initialization dependency, add regression coverage for consent states, and keep production console error-free.

findings.summary: Platform hygiene prevents BFCache and omits source maps
findings.evidence: Lighthouse reported a BFCache blocker and two large first-party JavaScript files without valid source maps.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove unload/BFCache blockers and publish production source maps with controlled access for diagnosability.

findings.summary: Some interactive anchors are not crawlable links
findings.evidence: Lighthouse found three <a> controls without href, including audio and live-bet affordances.
findings.suggestedFix: Use buttons for actions or provide real destination href values for navigation links.

findings.summary: Entity pages lack structured data
findings.evidence: The platform probe found zero JSON-LD blocks, including on match and article archetypes that map naturally to SportsEvent and NewsArticle entities.
findings.suggestedFix: Add accurate JSON-LD for NewsArticle and SportsEvent and validate it against visible content.

findings.summary: The sampled article lacks a meta description
findings.evidence: The article discoverability capture reports metaDescriptionPresentInRaw: null although its title and H1 are available.
findings.suggestedFix: Generate a unique article meta description and matching Open Graph description from the article standfirst.

findings.summary: Core defensive response headers are absent
findings.evidence: The headers primitive found no CSP, HSTS, X-Content-Type-Options, clickjacking protection, Referrer-Policy, or Permissions-Policy.
findings.suggestedFix: Deploy a tested CSP, HSTS, nosniff, frame-ancestors, strict referrer policy, and a least-privilege Permissions-Policy.

findings.summary: Tracking and consent scope are disproportionate
findings.evidence: The page contacts 11 third-party origins and four known trackers; HAR attributes 1.29 MB and 67 requests to third parties, while consent copy names 1001 partners.
findings.suggestedFix: Minimise vendors and purposes, block trackers until consent, batch essential analytics, and document a strict data-minimisation budget.

findings.summary: Browser-enforced security policies are not configured
findings.evidence: The headers evidence shows no HSTS, clickjacking control, Referrer-Policy, Permissions-Policy, or CSP frame-ancestors.
findings.suggestedFix: Add and monitor defensive headers at the edge; start CSP in report-only mode and tighten it before enforcement.

findings.summary: Core score content is only partially available without JavaScript
findings.evidence: Discoverability coverage was 36% on home and 54% on match; the match H1 was absent from raw HTML, although neither page was an empty JS shell.
findings.suggestedFix: Server-render primary score/match identity content and progressively enhance live updates.

findings.summary: The consent experience is a nagging wall with extreme vendor scope
findings.evidence: Every fresh results-page load presents a full consent wall describing 1001 partners before the core task; reject is visible, but the interruption and scope undermine freely given, proportionate consent.
findings.suggestedFix: Reduce vendor scope and present concise, purpose-level consent without blocking score access; preserve an equally prominent reject choice.

findings.summary: Images use legacy formats without responsive delivery metadata
findings.evidence: The images probe found 100 legacy PNG/JPEG images, zero modern formats, 100 missing dimensions, and four missing srcset attributes.
findings.suggestedFix: Serve AVIF/WebP where beneficial, retain fallback formats, provide responsive sources, and declare dimensions.

findings.summary: Third-party work is heavy relative to the score-listing task
findings.evidence: HAR recorded 67 third-party requests and 1.29 MB third-party bytes, including multiple analytics and ad stacks before the user engages.
findings.suggestedFix: Set a third-party byte/request budget, defer optional vendors until interaction/consent, and remove duplicate analytics destinations.

findings.summary: Background and startup work is not proportionate
findings.evidence: The page starts 109 requests and 42 scripts; Lighthouse TBT is 900 ms and the reduced-motion probe still found many continuously running shimmer animations.
findings.suggestedFix: Pause animation and refresh work when hidden/reduced-motion is active, and schedule non-essential fetching at low priority.

findings.summary: The initial memory footprint is unusually large for a score listing
findings.evidence: The baseline heap summary contains 937,483 nodes, 4.31 million edges, and 62.5 MB self size, including 341,536 native nodes and 64,797 closures.
findings.suggestedFix: Reduce DOM virtualization scope, unload hidden league/template trees, and lazy-initialize optional widgets and vendor code.

findings.summary: Heap grows substantially after repeated consent interaction
findings.evidence: The post-interaction heap rose from 62.5 MB/937,483 nodes to 92.5 MB/1,392,771 nodes (+48% bytes, +49% nodes); separate page sessions lower confidence, so confirm with same-session GC snapshots before treating as a proven leak.
findings.suggestedFix: Repeat baseline/target/final snapshots in one session with forced GC, then trace retained consent nodes/listeners and dispose them on close.
